info.bio:
Echo & the Bunnymen (EATB) es una banda británica de post-punk formada en Liverpool en 1978. La formación original la constituían Ian McCulloch (de los Crucial Three), Will Sergeant y Les Pattinson, complementados por una caja de ritmos que muchos dedujeron que era "Echo", aunque la banda lo niega.

Cuando lanzaron su álbum de debut en 1980, Crocodiles, un éxito moderado en ventas el Reino Unido, la caja de ritmos se reemplazó por Pete de Freitas.

scenes.name: Nueva psicodelia y big music: Echo & the Bunnymen y U2
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En lugar de descender a lo oscuro, elevarse hacia la luz. Liverpool, que no tuvo punk clásico ni postpunk experimental, quería que la música fuera «una fiesta» (Bill Drummond, Zoo): el club Eric's, las bandas fantasma (The Crucial Three, Big in Japan), Wah! Heat, The Teardrop Explodes de Julian Cope. Echo & the Bunnymen, con el minimalismo aprendido de Television y la voz de Ian McCulloch, graban Crocodiles y Heaven Up Here, respuesta luminosa a Closer, y heredan el público huérfano de Joy Division; Ocean Rain los vuelve estrellas pop. U2, «punk positivo» cristiano y pacifista, guitarra de The Edge como sintetizador, quiere ocupar el lugar de Curtis: War (1983), «Sunday Bloody Sunday» en MTV, The Unforgettable Fire con Eno. Alrededor, la «big music» celta de Simple Minds, The Waterboys, Big Country y la neopsicodelia de The Blue Orchids.

scenes.name: Revival psicodélico y garage de los ochenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El revival más persistente de los ochenta y noventa. En Los Ángeles, el «Paisley Underground»: Rain Parade, Three O'Clock, Dream Syndicate (síntesis de Dylan y la Velvet), Savage Republic, True West, Opal. En la Costa Este, los imitadores fetichistas (Lyres, Fuzztones, Chesterfield Kings) y bandas creativas (Das Damen, Plasticland, Eleventh Dream Day). El garage más crudo: Honeymoon Killers, Gibson Bros, Gories, Original Sins, God Bullies, Pandoras. La psicodelia libre de jams: Crystallized Movements, Magic Hour, Vocokesh, Sun City Girls, Black Sun Ensemble, Helios Creed. En Australia, Celibate Rifles, Died Pretty, Hoodoo Gurus, Beasts Of Bourbon, Scientists, Feedtime, Crime And The City Solution; en Europa, Hanoi Rocks, Echo & The Bunnymen, Teardrop Explodes, Bevis Frond, Legendary Pink Dots, The The y Love And Rockets.

podcast.title: "Echo" Drum Machine Name
podcast.body: Echo & the Bunnymen initially relied on a small, affordable Korg Mini Pops Jr. drum machine, which sold for under $150. This unit eventually earned the nickname "Echo," which contributed to the band's own name. "It is the Echo in Echo in the Bunnyman."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the Drum Machine

podcast.title: Drum Machine Use
podcast.body: Echo & the Bunnymen utilized a drum machine in their performances, rather than a flesh-and-blood drummer. This reflects a broader trend in the 1980s where electronic rhythm devices began to replace or augment traditional drummers. "The echo and echo in the bunny-man is actually a drum machine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: John Hughes Film Exposure (1980s)
podcast.body: Echo & The Bunnymen's music was included on the carefully selected soundtracks of John Hughes' 1980s films. These soundtracks were vital in introducing many people, particularly in North America, to a variety of alternative rock bands, especially those from the UK. "So many people learned of bands like The Specials and Spandovalet and Billy Idle and General Public and Wang Chung and Yellow and New Order and the Psychedelic Furs and the Smiths and Echo and the Bunyman, Susanne Vagan in excess the Jesus and Mary chain, Flesh for Luluo and so many others from those soundtrack albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Managed by Bill Drummond
podcast.body: In their early days, Echo and the Bunnyman were managed by Bill Drummond, who would later co-found The KLF. "Drummond used to be the manager of Echo and the Bunnyman in the early days."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Peele Sessions Recordings (70s, 80s, 90s)
podcast.body: Echo & The Bunnymen (referred to as "Equivalent of the Buntyman") were part of the hundreds of bands that recorded "Peele Sessions" live at the BBC throughout the 70s, 80s, and 90s. These sessions were instrumental in allowing bands to be broadcast despite the BBC's "Needle Time" restrictions. "The Smiths, R.E.M., New Order, the Fall, Equivalent of the Buntyman, Susie the Banshee, the Bus Cox, the list is almost endless."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Music vs Technology Over The Years

podcast.title: Shift to Human Drummers
podcast.body: As the band developed, the Korg Mini Pops Jr. (affectionately called "poor little Echo") was replaced by a human drummer. This human drummer then coexisted with another drum machine, the Roland TR-77. "But once the band got good enough, poor little Echo was ditched in favor of a human drummer, who by the way coexisted with another unit called the Roland TR-77."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the Drum Machine

podcast.title: Sire Records Signing
podcast.body: Echo & the Bunnymen were signed by Seymour Stein to Sire Records, demonstrating his interest in new post-punk music from the UK and Ireland. Sire Records leveraged the "New Wave" term for marketing these bands in North America. "echoing the bunny-man."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 5: New Wave

xref.title: Music as Escape and Teenage Influences
xref.body: Following a football injury that sidelined him for much of a season, music became Scott Weiland's primary escape. His favorite bands during this period included Depeche Mode, The Clash, Social Distortion, The Sweet, Echo & The Bunnymen, and Queen. "Music became his escape, especially after a football injury forced him to sit out much of a season."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Musical Influences
xref.body: The Bravery incorporated elements from Depeche Mode, The Cure, Echo & the Bunnymen, The Cars, and Duran Duran to create a sound that felt both new and familiar. Their music, released in 2005, prompted rhetorical questions about whether it was from 2005 or 1980. "They took bits of Depeche Mode, the cure, echo in the bunnyman, the cars, and Durand-Dorand to come up with something new yet very familiar."
